in other words, a walk leaving the lourdes grotto at st patrick's church at 10.00am and proceeding by the ballyfounder road to st. cooey's wells and onto bankmore and cook st and returning to st. patrick’s. enroute there would be stops near ballytrustan graveyard, at st. cooey's wells, n ear the mass rock at ballyedock and back to the lourdes grotto. at each stop the parti cipants could pray for the holy souls, if they wish. everything would be done from the public road apart froma visit to the wells where toilets will be available. to avoid a large bunch of people, the walkers would setoff in small groups of 4 or 5 at five- minute intervals from st. patrick’s. this will not be a large procession of pilgrims but, as stated, small groups of 4 or 5 friends. permission has been sought from the parades commission. we need people who do intend to go on the walk to act as stewards at road junctions; the belfast jesuit centre will host a special hybrid book launch on monday 19 october at 7.00pm for conquest or leaven: reflections of a catholic priest in palestine/israel by fr david neuhaus sj. join us for a short talk from the author, a guided conversation, and live q&a with fr neuhaus who will join us via live video link. his story - from south african jewish roots to christian faith and jesuit ministry in the holy land - offers a powerful and unique perspective on justice, p eace, and human dignity. books will be available at a discounted rate. visit

to register. we look forward to welcoming you to this thoughtful and urgent conversation. pips charity is a regional northern ireland charity dedicated to suicide prevention, supporting mental health and emotional wellbeing. with offices in belfast, derry and enniskillen, we p rovide a range of free support services, such as crisis intervention, counselling, and befriending, to individuals and families affected by suicidal thoughts, emotional distress, mental health difficulties, and bereavement. we would particularly like to bring your attention to our weekend crisis hopeline, a regional overnight telephone service available friday and sunday nights, to anyone across northern ireland experiencing emotional distress, suicidal thoughts, or a mental health crisis. the operational hours for the weekend crisis hopeline are as follows. friday: 9pm - 10am saturday sunday: 9pm - 9am monday

| freephone 0800 088 6042 we know that crisis doesn't wait for working hours. the weekend crisis hopeline provides a confidential, non-judgemental space to talk with a trained crisis practitioner when someone is in distress, needs support or simply wants someone to talk to during a difficult time outside of working hours. there is no referral process for the hopeline, and individuals can contact us directly whenever they feel in need of support. for more information, please feel free to refer to our website where the information on the weekend crisis hopeline is posted: weekend crisis hopeline - pips suicide prevention ireland
